classes.name: Volby do Poslanecké sněmovny Parlamentu České republiky
classes.finest_note: Polling-district (okrsek) counts in the open data from 2002; 1996 and 1998 are HTML tables by obec. Okrsky are lists of addresses; their outlines are drawn from RÚIAN address points.
classes.note: 200 seats by list PR. 1996 and 1998: 8 electoral regions (the former kraje), D'Hondt at national level after Hagenbach-Bischoff in the regions. 2002–2017: the 14 kraje with D'Hondt in each. Since 2021 (Act 189/2021 after Constitutional Court ruling Pl. ÚS 44/17): Imperiali quota in the kraje, then Hagenbach-Bischoff on pooled remainders; thresholds 5%, 8%, and 11%. The Czech National Council elected in 1992 became the first Chamber on 1 January 1993.

cadence.administered_by: Ministerstvo vnitra; results by Český statistický úřad; Státní volební komise
cadence.vacancy_rule: A seat falls to the next candidate on the same list (§ 28); the Chamber can be dissolved under čl. 35, giving early elections (1998 and 2013).

classes.finest_note: Polling-district counts in the open data from 2008 and in the cumulative 1996–2025 file; earlier dates by obec.
classes.note: 81 single-member districts (Annex 3 of Act 247/1995); a third elected every two years for six-year terms; two-round majority, the runoff a week after the first round between the top two. All 81 seats in 1996. Vacancies are filled by by-elections (doplňovací volby).

classes.name: Volby do zastupitelstev obcí
classes.finest_note: Polling-district counts with each candidate's votes in the open data from 2002; 1990, 1994, and 1998 are HTML tables by obec. A council may be split into several electoral districts.
classes.note: Councils of every obec, town, městys, statutory city, and the capital (Zastupitelstvo hlavního města Prahy). The councils of the city districts of Prague and the statutory cities are the separate class zmc. Open lists with up to as many votes as seats; 5% threshold, D'Hondt. New, supplementary, and repeat elections between the regular ones are called by Ministry of Interior notices. The 1990 count is the source's single figure and may include city-district councils, which cannot be told apart in the 1990 HTML.

cadence.vacancy_rule: Substitutes from the list; when a council falls below its members or is dissolved, new elections (nové volby) are held (§ 58 of Act 491/2001)

classes.name: Volby do zastupitelstev městských částí a městských obvodů
classes.name_en: City-district council elections (Prague and the statutory cities)
classes.finest_note: Polling-district counts with each candidate's votes in the open data from 2002; 1994 and 1998 are HTML tables by city district. A council may be split into several electoral districts. Districts are drawn as the union of the RÚIAN polling districts that carry the district's code; a district without a council has no area.
classes.note: Councils of the city districts (městské části) of Prague and the city districts (městské obvody) of statutory cities: 132 in 1994, 134 in 1998, 140 since 2006, as the Ministry of Interior's notices and the open data's council list count them. The open data's 2002 council list also marks 9 ordinary villages as district councils; they are counted under zo. Open lists with up to as many votes as seats; 5% threshold, D'Hondt.

cadence.administered_by: Ministerstvo vnitra and the municipal offices; results by Český statistický úřad
cadence.vacancy_rule: Substitutes from the list; when a council falls below its members or is dissolved, new elections (nové volby) are held (§ 58 of Act 491/2001)

classes.name: Místní referendum
classes.note: Held by obce and city districts under Act 298/1992 and since 2004 Act 22/2004 (valid at 35% turnout, binding with a majority that is at least 25% of the electorate). The Ministry of Interior table lists 569 announced referendums since 2006 with turnout and yes and no counts.

access.evidence: One row per referendum: obec, question, date, turnout, yes and no votes, and whether the result binds.

classes.name: Volby do národních výborů
classes.name_en: National committee elections (local, district, and regional), 1954–1986
classes.note: Single-list elections to the local, town, district, and regional national committees in 1954, 1957, 1960, 1964, 1971, 1976, 1981, and 1986.
classes.disposition_reason: No official digital publication of the returns was found on volby.cz or csu.gov.cz; only national totals were printed at the time.

classes.name: Volby do obecních, okresních a zemských zastupitelstev 1919–1938
classes.name_en: Municipal, district, and land assembly elections of the First Republic
classes.note: Municipal elections from 1919 (staggered, mostly 1919, 1923, 1927, 1931, and 1938) and the district and land assemblies of Bohemia and Moravia-Silesia in 1928 and 1935.
classes.disposition_reason: No official digital publication of the returns was found; they are in printed State Statistical Office volumes and municipal records.

classes.name: Nepřímé volby orgánů
classes.name_en: Indirect elections by councils and Parliament
classes.disposition_reason: Officers chosen by elected bodies, not by voters: mayors (starosta, primátor) and boards by municipal councils, the hejtman and regional board by regional councils, lay judges by councils, and the speakers of both chambers; no electorate votes.

classes.name: Osadní a místní výbory
classes.name_en: Settlement committees of parts of obce
classes.disposition_reason: Appointed by the municipal council (§ 120 of Act 128/2000: členy osadního výboru určuje zastupitelstvo obce); residents' meetings only propose members.

classes.name: Volby samosprávných komor, škol a stran
classes.name_en: Chamber, school board, university, workplace, and party elections
classes.disposition_reason: Run by the bodies themselves for their members: professional and agricultural chambers, school boards (školské rady), university senates, works councils, and party candidate selections. No state-run nominating contest exists; candidates are nominated by parties, movements, and petitions.
